2026-04-10.brief: April tenth was a heavy implementation day. The system's self-awareness layer was built out in earnest. One agent was split into a pair that separately handles stated assumptions and unstated presumptions, and a literature search agent was split into independent for-and-against searchers to prevent confirmation bias. A baseline metrics snapshot was captured, and a provenance protocol was written to track every premise's chain of custody.
2026-04-10.deep: April tenth answered a question that had been building through Tom's review cycles: how does a system reason honestly about its own premises? The answer took the form of infrastructure. The original extraction agent was split into two, one that pulls out assumptions the designers knew they were making and another that surfaces presumptions taken for granted without awareness. The literature search agent was similarly split into independent for-and-against searchers, so neither could be biased by the other's first findings. A net evaluator and a periodic monitor were added to close the loop with three dispositions: incorporate, monitor, or flag for revision. A provenance protocol was written so every premise carries its chain of custody and its epistemic tag. All eleven tradition agent dispatches gained reference-frame-location and conceptual-bearing fields, implementing the Thousand Brains principle at the communication layer. A baseline metrics snapshot fixed Stage Zero of a six-stage maturity model. The day mattered because the system moved from asking about the traditions to asking about itself, with an auditable pipeline rather than a rhetorical promise.

2026-04-13.brief: April thirteenth was the day C2A2's self-awareness machinery closed its first full loop. Twenty-five claims about the system's own architecture passed through paired supportive and adversarial literature searches and came back dispositioned. The verdict was uncomfortable: role-assignment bias, multi-agent coordination overhead, and the validity of cross-tradition signals all took serious hits. Meanwhile, the wiki pipeline had been silently failing for four straight days.
2026-04-13.deep: April thirteenth was operationally messy and epistemically sharp. Fourteen new proposals arrived from Levin, Friston, Stump, Fredrickson, Carroll, Arkani-Hamed, and Wolfram, mostly catch-up from missed weekend runs, pushing the review backlog past thirty-seven. But the real event was the first full turn of the self-awareness pipeline. Twenty-five claims the system had surfaced about its own architecture were sent through two independent literature searches, one looking for support and one looking for challenge, then reconciled and dispositioned. Three were cleared as validated. Fifteen went to a monitor queue. Seven were flagged for revision. The challenges clustered in uncomfortable places: the for-and-against agent structure may amplify the biases it was designed to counter; multi-agent coordination overhead likely exceeds what the architecture assumed; and most troublingly, the core value proposition, the claim that agents can reliably distinguish structural cross-tradition signals from surface resemblance, rests on a distinction that the literature says is empirically hard to validate. An evening run then surfaced assumptions about the pipeline itself, including the self-referential circularity of using the pipeline to evaluate the pipeline. Underneath all this, the wiki daily run had failed for four consecutive days on an auth error, with no alerting to catch it.
